review.tagline: Node.js backend with REST and GraphQL APIs on MongoDB or PostgreSQL
review.summary: Parse Server is a self-hosted backend that runs on Node.js, either standalone via the parse-server CLI or mounted on an Express app. It exposes REST and GraphQL APIs backed by MongoDB or PostgreSQL (with PostGIS), and adds Cloud Code, Live Query, push notifications, file adapters and per-key access scopes. Official Parse SDKs cover the major client platforms.
review.audience: Developers self-hosting a REST/GraphQL backend for mobile and web apps
strengths: Runs standalone or embedded in an existing Express app
Supports both MongoDB (7, 8) and PostgreSQL (16-18) with PostGIS
Includes Cloud Code, Live Query, GraphQL, push and pluggable file storage adapters
Fine-grained access scopes: master, read-only master, session and maintenance keys
weaknesses: No built-in admin UI in this repo; a separate dashboard project is needed
Requires you to provision and operate your own MongoDB or PostgreSQL
Docker image must be built from the repo; README shows no prebuilt image or compose file
Node.js version support is tied to specific majors and shifts with each release
needs: Needs Node.js 20, 22 or 24, MongoDB 7/8 or PostgreSQL 16-18 with PostGIS
